title: feat(cli): name enterprise and cloud capabilities no provider enforces in os validate, os verify and os serve
body:
Fixes #34726

Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:`os verify` 现在会跑 `os validate` 已有的「能力提供方检查」并以提示(advisory)形式输出(`--json` 新增 `capabilities` 字段);`os validate` / `os build` 增加「已安装但没接进 `plugins[]`」的检查;企业版能力的提示写明后果(层级可见范围在开源版按「只看自己的记录」处理);`os serve` 启动时对没有提供方的企业版/云端能力打印一行提示。
- 为什么改:声明了 `requires: ['hierarchy-security']` 却没有企业版提供方时,`os verify` 全绿、`os serve` 无声、运行时静默退回 owner-only,开发者无从得知;按维护者指示「os verify 点名企业版能力」。
- 风险与回滚:只增加提示;默认退出码不变(`os verify` 对云端能力仍为 0,与 `os validate` 的 exit 1 不一致,见 Acceptance notes)。唯一例外是 `os validate --strict`:它本来就把所有警告当失败,所以「装了企业包但没接进 `plugins[]`」(或包装上了却加载失败)的应用,在 `--strict` 下会从 exit 0 变成 exit 1;不加 `--strict` 和 `os build` 不受影响;运行时行为不变,仍 fail-closed;回滚即 revert 本 PR。
- 先看:`packages/cli/src/utils/capability-preflight.ts`(`preflightProviderWiring` 与企业版后果文案)、`packages/cli/src/commands/verify.ts`(`runCapabilityAdvisories`)、`packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts`(启动提示,能力解析循环之前)。
- 两分钟验证:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli exec vitest run --project integration test/capability-edition-advisory.test.ts`,预期 2 个用例通过:开源版应用在 validate 与 verify `--json` 中都出现 `hierarchy-security` 提示,接上提供方后两边都没有。
- 需要你做的:无,席位落地。

## What changes

The capability registry (`PLATFORM_CAPABILITY_PROVIDERS`) already tags each `requires` token with an edition, and `os validate` already classified declared tokens against it (`packages/cli/src/utils/capability-preflight.ts`). This PR extends that one classifier; no new lint rule, no spec change.

1. **`os verify` surfaces the capability-provider check** (stage 1, after the author-time rules). Every finding `os validate` raises for a declared token is reported as an advisory: a line on the text face, and `capabilities: [{ token, message, validate }]` on the `--json` report, where `validate` is `error` when `os validate` refuses the stack over it and `warning` when it only reports it. `[]` when there is none. **The exit code is unchanged for every token**, cloud tokens included.
2. **Wiring check** (`preflightProviderWiring`), in `os validate`, `os build` and through (1) `os verify`. An `enterprise`-edition token whose package resolves but which no `plugins[]` entry provides is a warning. Nothing mounts an enterprise provider from `requires`, so a resolvable package alone enforces nothing. A `plugins[]` entry provides the token when it is an instance of a class the package exports (or carries that `name`), the exact identity match `serve` uses (`providesCapability`), or a string entry naming the package. A package that resolves but cannot be loaded is reported as `unloadable`, never read as wired. Which tokens are `enterprise` is the registry's edition tag.
3. **The enterprise message names the consequence.** For example: "Only the enterprise edition enforces it: without a wired provider, as on the open edition, the hierarchy scopes (`own_and_reports`, `unit`, `unit_and_below`) behave as owner-only, and no log line says so." The remedy reads "Install PKG and add its plugin to `plugins[]`, or remove the token from `requires`", in place of the old `pnpm add PKG`. `ENTERPRISE_ABSENCE_CONSEQUENCE` only sharpens that sentence; a future enterprise token with no row gets a generic consequence, and a test pins every row to an enterprise registry token.
4. **`os serve` start-up line.** A declared token with no resolver row and no tier block (today `hierarchy-security`, `ai-seat`, `governance`, `audit-compliance`, `access-policy-console`) used to pass the capability loop in silence. It now prints the same sentence once, as a warning, when nothing in `plugins[]` provides it. The boot is unchanged. `ai` / `ai-studio` already fail the boot through their tier block with the edition-aware message.
5. **Docs.** The permission pages that describe the hierarchy scopes (`index`, `permission-sets`, `permissions-matrix`, `positions`, `administrator-guide`) now say the enterprise edition enforces them and the open edition treats them as owner-only. `deployment/cli.mdx` documents verify's new stage and the `capabilities` field.

Runtime behaviour is unchanged: `SharingService.resolveOwnerScopeIds` still fails closed to owner-only without the resolver.

## Tests

- `packages/cli/test/capability-preflight.test.ts` (unit): a battery derived from the registry, one pair of cases per non-`open` token (7 today: `hierarchy-security` enterprise; `ai`, `ai-studio`, `ai-seat`, `governance`, `audit-compliance`, `access-policy-console` cloud) with a floor so an emptied registry cannot pass vacuously. No provider gives exactly one finding naming the token. Provider present gives none, except the packageless cloud tiers, which have no provider to be present. Wiring cases: plugins empty, unrelated plugin only, exported class present, string entry (never loads), unloadable, unresolved (not this check's finding), per-package attribution, open/cloud tokens never reach it. The consequence rows are pinned to enterprise tokens.
- `packages/cli/test/capability-edition-advisory.test.ts` (integration, spawned source CLI): the open-edition stack (`requires: ['hierarchy-security']` and a `unit_and_below` grant) gets the finding in `os validate --json` `warnings` and in `os verify --json` `capabilities`, the same sentence, both exit 0. The control, the same stack with a package of the provider's name declared and its exported plugin class in `plugins[]`, gets none from either door.
- Ledgers updated: `normalized-call-sites.test.ts` classifies verify's top-level `requires` read (handed to the same top-level-else-bodies rule); `validate-build-gate-parity.test.ts` lists `preflightProviderWiring` as a shared gate (wired into both `validate.ts` and `compile.ts`).

## Acceptance notes

- **validate/verify exit-code parity gap, the 6 cloud tokens** (`ai`, `ai-studio`, `ai-seat`, `governance`, `audit-compliance`, `access-policy-console`). `os validate` refuses such a stack with exit 1; `os verify` now reports the same sentence under `capabilities` with `validate: 'error'` but still exits 0, by this card's ruling (advisory only). Whether `os verify` should match `os validate`'s exit 1 is a separate decision: filed #35170.
- **Runtime silence stays.** The sharing layer's owner-only fallback (`SharingService.resolveOwnerScopeIds`, `if (!resolver) return [me];`) still logs nothing; the CLI now says it at start-up for `os serve`, but a host that boots without the CLI (cloud's objectos-runtime) gets no line from this change. Filed #35172.
- **Wiring heuristic.** A `plugins[]` instance of ANY class the provider package exports counts as wired. `@objectstack/security-enterprise` exports several plugins (`SecurityEnterprisePlugin` registers the hierarchy resolver; others such as the AI-seat plugin do not), so wiring only an unrelated plugin from that package silences the warning. The registry carries no plugin identity per token; tightening this needs a registry field (spec, out of this card's surface). Filed #35173.
- **The wiring check loads the provider package** (only for a declared enterprise token whose package resolves), through `serve`'s host importer. `os serve` already loads it on boot; `os validate` / `os build` now do too in that one case.
- **`os build` gets the wiring warning as well**: the closed gate-parity ledger requires a gate in `validate.ts` to be in `compile.ts` too or recorded as a validate-only gap; wiring it in both was the smaller change.
- **Skills follow-up**: the `skills/**` text describing hierarchy scopes (which edition enforces them, and the new verify `capabilities` field) is follow-up card #35171; `skills/**` is not edited here.
- Gates: `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack --commands` derived 106 families at 528e8c1; all 106 exit 0 (each exit code captured before any pipe). `--ran` reconciliation: "106 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 106 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED". The other CI families (artifact rosters, wide-population, type-check lanes, Build Core, dogfood) are CI's.

## Verification

Manual readings at 45f1303 (source CLI, `bin/run-dev.js`), fixtures in a temp dir:

- open stack: `os validate --json` exit 0, one `warnings` entry for `hierarchy-security` naming owner-only; `os verify --json` exit 0, `capabilities` holds the same sentence, `hardFailures` 0.
- same stack, provider package installed but `plugins[]` empty: `os validate --json` exit 0 with the unwired warning; `os verify --json` the same under `capabilities`.
- provider wired: no capability finding from either door.
- `requires: ['governance', 'hierarchy-security']`: `os verify` text face prints both, the cloud one suffixed "`os validate` refuses this stack.", exit 0; `os serve --dev` prints both lines at start-up and boots (discovery 200); with the provider wired, `os serve` prints neither.
